en.name: Thyme, fresh
en.summary: Fresh thyme keeps 1–2 weeks at room temperature with the stems in water, and 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. The leaves are tiny, firm and oily, which is why thyme outlives the soft herbs by a wide margin.
en.pantry: 1–2 weeks with the stem ends trimmed and standing in a jar of water, out of direct sunlight, with the water changed daily. Like rosemary and oregano, thyme is a Mediterranean plant that copes with dry air; on the counter it dries out rather than rotting, and a bunch that has dried on its own is simply dried thyme. Trim the stems each time you change the water so the cut ends do not turn slimy.
en.fridge: 2–3 weeks at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, wrapped loosely in dry kitchen paper inside a bag or a box in the crisper. Do not wash it before storing: the leaves sit so close to the stem that trapped water has nowhere to go, and a bunch sealed damp will blacken quickly. Replace the paper if it feels wet, and pull out any blackened sprigs so they do not take the rest with them.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for fresh thyme. Freezing does work in practice — strip the leaves, spread them on a tray, then bag them, or freeze whole sprigs and crumble the leaves off while still frozen, which is easier than stripping them fresh. The flavour survives because it is carried in stable resinous oils, but the texture does not, so use frozen thyme only in cooked dishes. For a surplus, drying is the traditional and better answer.
en.thawing: Do not thaw. Add frozen leaves or sprigs straight to the pot.
spoilage: Leaves turned black, usually starting where the bunch was tied.
A musty or sour smell instead of a warm, faintly medicinal one.
Slime on the lower stems or at the cut ends.
Mould on the stems inside a tightly sealed bag.
tips: Run the sprig backwards between finger and thumb to strip the leaves.
Do not bother chopping thyme leaves; they are already small enough.
Tie a few sprigs with parsley and a bay leaf for a bouquet garni you can fish out later.
Dry a surplus bunch upside down in an airy spot rather than losing it in the fridge.

faq.q: How long does fresh thyme keep?
faq.a: 1–2 weeks at room temperature with the stems in water, or 2–3 weeks refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
No freezer timeline is published for it. Freezing works well enough in practice for cooked dishes — frozen sprigs are actually easier to strip — but drying is the more useful route.

faq.q: Do you have to strip thyme leaves off the stem?
faq.a: Not for a stew or a stock; drop the sprig in whole and remove the bare stem afterwards. Strip it when the leaves need to stay in the dish.

zh.name: 新鮮百里香
zh.summary: 新鮮百里香把莖插在水裡放室溫可放 1～2 週，放 4 °C 以下冷藏則是 2～3 週。它的葉片細小、結實又含油，所以耐放程度遠遠超過軟莖香草。
zh.pantry: 把莖的切口剪一下、插進水瓶，避開直曬、每天換水，可放 1～2 週。和迷迭香、奧勒岡一樣，百里香是地中海植物，不怕乾燥空氣；它在檯面上會慢慢乾掉而不是爛掉，而一把自己乾掉的百里香，就是乾燥百里香。每次換水時順手把切口剪掉一小截，免得發黏。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 2～3 週：用乾的廚房紙巾鬆鬆包好，裝進袋子或盒子放蔬果室。收之前不要洗——葉片貼著莖長，卡進去的水出不來，一把濕著密封的百里香很快就會發黑。紙巾摸起來濕了就換，並把已經發黑的枝條挑掉，免得拖累其他的。
zh.freezer: 新鮮百里香沒有公布的冷凍期限。實際上冷凍是行得通的——把葉子剝下來攤在盤子上凍硬再裝袋，或者整枝冷凍、要用時趁冰硬把葉子搓下來，反而比新鮮時好剝。風味撐得住，因為它靠的是穩定的樹脂類精油；口感撐不住，所以冷凍百里香只適合用在需要加熱的菜裡。量太多的話，傳統的陰乾還是比較好的答案。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍。冷凍的葉子或枝條直接丟進鍋裡。
spoilage: 葉子發黑，通常從綁束的地方先開始。
聞起來有霉味或酸味，而不是溫暖、微帶藥草感的香氣。
下段的莖或切口變得黏滑。
密封太緊的袋子裡，莖上長霉。
tips: 用拇指和食指逆著枝條往下擼，葉子就下來了。
百里香葉不必再切，它本來就夠小。
和巴西里、月桂葉綁成一束香草束，煮完整束撈掉很方便。
多出來的整束倒掛在通風處陰乾，好過在冰箱裡慢慢忘掉它。

faq.q: 新鮮百里香可以放多久？
faq.a: 莖插水放室溫 1～2 週，或 4 °C 以下冷藏 2～3 週。

faq.q: 新鮮百里香可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 它沒有公布冷凍期限。實務上用在熟食裡是可行的，冷凍後的枝條反而更好剝葉；但陰乾是更實用的做法。

faq.q: 百里香一定要把葉子剝下來嗎？
faq.a: 燉菜或熬高湯不必，整枝丟進去、煮完把光莖撈出來就好。需要讓葉子留在菜裡時才剝。
